hints: Focus on what makes a carbon chiral, a single carbon joined to four completely different atoms or groups.
Draw the product of each reaction quickly and look for any carbon with two identical methyl groups, as that can never be chiral.
Check the addition to the aldehyde, the new carbon gains H, OH, CN and an ethyl group, so count how many different groups it has.
walkthrough:
**Recall the test for chirality**

A chiral carbon is bonded to four different atoms or groups. If any two groups are the same, it is achiral.

Rule to use:
$$\text{chiral C} = \text{C attached to 4 different groups}$$

**Draw each product**

Let us work out what each pair makes. Addition to the alkene, reduction of the ketone, addition to the aldehyde, and esterification.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CH}_2 + \text{HBr} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CHBrCH}_3$$
$$\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{C=O} \xrightarrow{\text{NaBH}_4} \text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{CHOH}$$
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO} + \text{HCN} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CN}$$
$$\text{CH}_3\text{COOH} + \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_3$$

**Check for four different groups**

In $\text{CH}_3\text{CHBrCH}_3$ the middle C has two identical $\text{CH}_3$ groups, so not chiral. In $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{CHOH}$ the middle C also has two identical $\text{CH}_3$ groups, so not chiral. The ester $\text{CH}_3\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_3$ has no carbon with four different single bonds.

Only $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CN}$ has a carbon joined to H, OH, CN and $\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, four different groups, so it is chiral.

options.A: Product is 2-bromopropane, $\text{CH}_3\text{CHBrCH}_3$. The C-Br carbon is bonded to two identical $\text{CH}_3$ groups plus H and Br, so it has only three distinct groups and is achiral.
options.B: Product is propan-2-ol, $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{CHOH}$. The central carbon is bonded to two identical $\text{CH}_3$ groups, so it cannot be chiral. Reduction of a symmetrical ketone like propanone never creates chirality.
options.C: Product is the cyanohydrin $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CN}$. The new carbon is bonded to four different groups: H, OH, CN and $\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. It is therefore a chiral centre, formed as a racemic mixture.
options.D: Product is the ester ethyl ethanoate, $\text{CH}_3\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_3$. No carbon in this molecule is attached to four different groups, so there is no chiral carbon.
